questions.answer: Use the chain rule \(\frac{dz}{dt}=z_x\frac{dx}{dt}+z_y\frac{dy}{dt}\). Here \(z_x=2x\), \(z_y=2y\), \(dx/dt=1\), and \(dy/dt=2\). Thus \(dz/dt=2x+4y\). Substituting \(x=t\) and \(y=2t\) gives \(dz/dt=2t+8t=10t\).

Using the chain rule, \(\frac{dz}{dt}=z_xx'(t)+z_yy'(t)\). Since \(z_x=y\), \(z_y=x\), \(x'=2t\), and \(y'=1\), we get \(dz/dt=y(2t)+x\). Substitute \(x=t^2\) and \(y=t+1\): \(dz/dt=2t(t+1)+t^2=3t^2+2t\).

questions.prompt: Let \(z=e^{xy}\), where \(x=s+t\) and \(y=s-t\). Find \(\partial z/\partial s\).
questions.answer: Use \(z_s=z_xx_s+z_yy_s\). We have \(z_x=ye^{xy}\), \(z_y=xe^{xy}\), \(x_s=1\), and \(y_s=1\). Therefore \(z_s=(y+x)e^{xy}\). Substituting \(x=s+t\) and \(y=s-t\), \(x+y=2s\) and \(xy=(s+t)(s-t)=s^2-t^2\), so \(z_s=2s e^{s^2-t^2}\).

questions.prompt: Let \(z=x^2y\), where \(x=r\cos\theta\) and \(y=r\sin\theta\). Find \(\partial z/\partial r\).
questions.answer: Use \(z_r=z_xx_r+z_yy_r\). Here \(z_x=2xy\), \(z_y=x^2\), \(x_r=\cos\theta\), and \(y_r=\sin\theta\). Thus \(z_r=2xy\cos\theta+x^2\sin\theta\). Substituting \(x=r\cos\theta\) and \(y=r\sin\theta\) gives \(z_r=3r^2\cos^2\theta\sin\theta\).
The chain rule gives \(dw/dt=w_xx'+w_yy'+w_zz'\). Since \(w_x=w_y=w_z=1\), and \(x'=1\), \(y'=2t\), \(z'=3t^2\), we get \(dw/dt=1+2t+3t^2\). This matches direct substitution \(w=t+t^2+t^3\).

questions.prompt: Let \(z=\ln(x+y)\), where \(x=u^2\) and \(y=v^2\). Find \(\partial z/\partial u\).
questions.answer: Use \(z_u=z_xx_u+z_yy_u\). Since \(y=v^2\) does not depend on \(u\), \(y_u=0\). Also \(z_x=1/(x+y)\) and \(x_u=2u\). Therefore \(z_u=\frac{1}{x+y}(2u)+\frac{1}{x+y}(0)=\frac{2u}{u^2+v^2}\).

questions.prompt: Let \(z=f(x,y)\), where \(x=s^2+t\) and \(y=st\). Express \(\partial z/\partial t\) in terms of \(f_x\) and \(f_y\).
questions.answer: For a composite \(z=f(x(s,t),y(s,t))\), the chain rule is \(z_t=f_xx_t+f_yy_t\). Here \(x_t=1\) and \(y_t=s\). Therefore \(\partial z/\partial t=f_x+s f_y\), with \(f_x\) and \(f_y\) evaluated at \((x,y)=(s^2+t,st)\).

questions.prompt: Let \(z=x^2+y^2\), where \(x=u+v\) and \(y=u-v\). Find \(\partial z/\partial v\).
questions.answer: Use \(z_v=z_xx_v+z_yy_v\). We have \(z_x=2x\), \(z_y=2y\), \(x_v=1\), and \(y_v=-1\). Thus \(z_v=2x-2y\). Substituting \(x=u+v\) and \(y=u-v\) gives \(z_v=2(u+v)-2(u-v)=4v\).

questions.prompt: A differentiable function \(z=f(x,y)\) has \(f_x(2,1)=5\) and \(f_y(2,1)=-3\). If \(x=t^2+1\) and \(y=t\), find \(dz/dt\) at \(t=1\).
questions.answer: At \(t=1\), \(x=1^2+1=2\) and \(y=1\), so the given partial derivatives apply. The chain rule gives \(dz/dt=f_xx'+f_yy'\). Here \(x'=2t\), so \(x'(1)=2\), and \(y'=1\). Therefore \(dz/dt=5(2)+(-3)(1)=7\).
